sections.presenting_complaint: Review of low mood, 4 weeks after starting sertraline.
sections.history: Low mood for about 3 months. Slight improvement in mornings only; mood 2–3/10. Early morning waking at 4 am. Reduced appetite with approximately half a stone weight loss. Works as a warehouse supervisor; currently signed off for a further two weeks. Reports passive suicidal ideation (would be easier not to wake up) most days for the last two weeks. No active suicidal thoughts, plans or preparations. No previous self-harm or suicide attempts. Protective factors: nephew and mother. Alcohol: about four pints a week. No drug use. Mild nausea in first week of sertraline, now resolved; no agitation. Attended with sister, with consent.
sections.medications_allergies: Sertraline 50 mg once daily (4 weeks). No known drug allergies.
sections.examination: Appears tired, reduced eye contact, slowed speech. Speech coherent. No psychotic features. PHQ-9: 19.
sections.impression: Moderately severe depression with partial response to sertraline. Passive suicidal ideation without plan or intent; protective factors present. Harmful alcohol use.
sections.plan: Increase sertraline to 100 mg once daily. Refer to NHS Talking Therapies and self-referral details given. Inform the community crisis team. Review in 4 weeks. Agreed to hand stockpiled medicines to sister. Alcohol support service details given; aim to reduce gradually.
